title: The teaching as teacher
hookLine: after I am gone, the dhamma and discipline will be your teacher

lines: PENCIL MARKS ON THE SHEET MUSIC.
DO THEY STILL HAVE A TEACHER?
cards: A piano teacher dies. Her students still have the exercises she wrote in pencil on their sheet music, the habits she drilled into their hands, the sound of her voice saying slower. Do they have a teacher anymore?
In one sense, no. In another, she's in every scale they play. The Buddha is lying between the sal trees, and before anyone asks, he names the question himself.

teach.h: WE HAVE NO TEACHER? DON'T SEE IT THAT WAY.
teach.b: It may be, Ananda, he says, that some of you will think: the teacher's word is over; we have no teacher. Don't see it that way.

teach.h: DHAMMA AND VINAYA WILL TEACH YOU.
teach.b: The Dhamma and the discipline that I have taught and laid down for you, that will be your teacher when I am gone. In Pali the pair is dhamma-vinaya: the teaching, and the training rules that shape a community's life.
Look at what he doesn't do.
He doesn't name a successor. He doesn't appoint a council. Earlier on this road he said he'd never thought of himself as the community's leader, and he stays consistent to the end.
The teacher becomes something anyone can open. Then come a few practical instructions, and then a remarkable invitation.
He asks the gathered monks: if any of you has a doubt or a question about the Buddha, the teaching, the community, the path or the practice, ask now.
Don't regret later that you were face to face with the teacher and didn't ask. Silence. He asks a second time.
Maybe you're holding back out of respect for me, he says; then tell a friend, and let the friend ask. Still silence. Ananda says it's wonderful: not one monk here has any doubt.
A teacher who could have closed with a speech instead spends his last minutes asking three times, is anything unclear?
If the teaching is going to be the teacher, it had better be understood.

how: Theravada monastics treat the Dhamma and Vinaya as their teacher, reciting the monastic rules every fortnight, and many Buddhist schools also honor living lineages of teachers who pass the teaching on.

o: the teaching and the discipline together
the final rules for choosing a council
a successor chosen to lead the monks

games.q: the teaching as teacher: tap the pairs.
p: not one monk has a doubt

s: the Buddha names a successor to lead the community
he says the Dhamma and discipline will be the teacher.
the Buddha asks three times whether anyone has a doubt
and suggests a shy monk could ask through a friend.
the monks ask many questions in the final hour
they stay silent; Ananda says no one has a doubt.

games.q: you're the Buddha, about to pass away. your students will soon think they have no teacher. what do you tell them?
o: choose the wisest among you to lead.
the teaching and the discipline I gave you will be your teacher.
games.why: the Dhamma and Vinaya will be their teacher. then he asks three times if anyone has a doubt.

practice: Sit as if a teacher you trust were in the room, not watching you critically, just present, and let your posture and breath settle the way they'd remind you to. Then let the picture go, and keep the posture and the breath.
What they taught is still here, in your back and in your lungs.

wordCard.voice: Dhamma-vinaya. The Buddha's words at Kusinara: when I am gone, the teaching and the discipline I taught will be your teacher. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali dhammavinaya: the teaching and the discipline, the Buddha's name for what he left behind.

carryVoice: Your line: the teaching is the teacher. No successor, just something anyone can open. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Digha Nikaya 16 (Mahaparinibbana Sutta), the Dhamma-Vinaya as teacher and the last questions
